title: Postfix Calculator
statement:
A calculator uses **postfix notation**: the operator comes after its two numbers. For example `3 4 +` means 3 + 4, and `2 3 4 * -` means 2 - (3 * 4).

The expression `expr` is a list of tokens separated by single spaces. A token is either a non-negative whole number or one of the operators `+`, `-`, `*`. The expression is always valid, and every intermediate result fits in a 32-bit integer.

Return the value of the expression.
constraints: tokens are separated by exactly one space; operators are + - *
the expression is valid and no value exceeds the 32-bit integer range

hints.nudge: When you read an operator, which two numbers does it use? Which numbers have you seen most recently?
hints.pattern: A stack of numbers: push numbers, pop two when you see an operator.
hints.walkthrough: Read the tokens left to right. A number is pushed onto the stack. An operator needs the two most recent numbers, which are on top of the stack: pop b (the right operand) then a (the left operand), compute a op b, and push the result back. Order matters for minus: it is a - b, not b - a. When the tokens run out, the single value left on the stack is the answer. O(n) time.
